summary: Fixes a duplicate assignment of RSVP message type values by changing the values for the Challenge and Integrity Response messages assigned in RFC 2747. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Two RSVP messages had been assigned the same type number. This RFC gives the Challenge and Integrity Response new numbers so that type 12 can identify the Bundle message.

questions: what message types did rfc 3097 change
subtitle: Renumbers two RSVP Integrity messages to resolve a conflict with the Bundle message.

tldr.problem: RFC 2747 and RFC 2961 assigned RSVP Message Type 12 to different messages: Integrity Response and Bundle.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes Challenge to type 25 and Integrity Response to type 26, leaving type 12 for Bundle.
tldr.outcome: Implementations following the change use 25 and 26 for the Integrity handshake; older and updated implementations do not interoperate with each other.

today: RFC 3097 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 2747. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A Duplicate Message Type
sections.content:
RFC 2747 assigns message type 12 to the Integrity Response. RFC 2961 assigns the same value to a Bundle message.

This memo says the refresh-reduction protocol was believed to have entered use before the conflict was noticed. It changes both Integrity message types to reduce possible interoperability problems.
sections.plainLanguage: Two different RSVP messages used the same number. The memo changes the Integrity handshake numbers to remove that conflict.

sections.title: New Challenge and Response Values
sections.content:
The Challenge message now has Message Type 25. The Integrity Response message now has Message Type 25+1, which is 26.

Changing the Challenge as well as its reply keeps the two messages identified as a matched handshake under the new assignments.
sections.plainLanguage: The Challenge uses type 25, and the Integrity Response uses type 26. Both messages receive new numbers as part of the fix.

sections.title: Compatibility Between Implementations
sections.content:
Two nodes that follow this change interoperate using type 12 for Bundle and types 25 and 26 for the Integrity handshake. A node that does not follow the change will not interoperate with one that does, although two older implementations can still interoperate as before.

The Integrity Response includes a 32-bit cookie that must match the Challenge. The memo says this prevents the handshake from succeeding accidentally because of the changed message numbers.
sections.plainLanguage: Updated nodes use the new numbers together, while older nodes keep the old assignments. The response must also carry a cookie matching the Challenge.
